title: Legal ledger: audit surface definition and crypto guardrails PRD + signoff checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD to define the legal and operational audit surface for Private/VPC deployments and to specify crypto guardrails (KMS/HSM integration, key rotation, key access policies), SSO/SAML assertion expectations, and RBAC audit trails. This doc clarifies scope changes requested by Legal and Compliance teams and provides an acceptance checklist for engineering, security, and compliance signoff.
background: Large enterprise customers and procurement/legal teams require a clear, auditable description of what data and control planes are visible to Redwood vs tenant operators for Private deployments. Recent RFPs requested explicit guarantees around KMS usage, key rotation proof, SAML assertion lifecycles, RBAC change history, and immutable audit ledger exports. This PRD consolidates those asks and converts them to implementation acceptance criteria.
scope: Define audit event taxonomy for: authentication (SSO/SAML), authorization (RBAC grants/revocations), key lifecycle (KMS/HSM create/rotate/destroy), admin actions (customer-managed configs), and system fallbacks.
Specify KMS/HSM integration modes supported (external KMS via customer key, Redwood-managed envelope keys with HSM-backed master key) and required audit bindings for each.
Define SSO/SAML artifact retention, replay-resistance expectations, and assertion validation logging required for audits.
Set RBAC change-tracking requirements: who changed, previous role, timestamp, IP/actor context, and post-change test traces.
Produce a signoff checklist for Legal, Security, and Engineering owners with required artifacts (logs, runbooks, test evidence).
out_of_scope: Encryption at rest algorithms beyond documented company-standard ciphers (we will not re-evaluate cryptographic algorithms in this ticket).
Migration automation for existing customer keys (a separate migration project will be scoped).
Full vendor HSM procurement — integrations assume common KMIP/Cloud KMS APIs.
requirements: REQ-01: Audit ledger must capture and immutably store events for SSO token validations, SAML assertions, and single-logout events with correlation IDs.

REQ-02: KMS/HSM events (key create, rotate, disable, destroy, use for unwrap) must be surfaced to the audit ledger, including the principal initiating the operation and the associated request context.
REQ-03: RBAC admin operations must persist a changelog entry with actor, timestamp, previous role set, new role set, and an automated post-change assertion test result.
REQ-04: Support exporting audit ledger slices (time-range or correlation-id) in JSON/CSV and providing signed manifests for legal evidence requests.
REQ-05: Provide a documented retention policy and configurable retention override for enterprise customers, with proof-of-deletion artifacts when requested.
REQ-06: SSO/SAML configuration changes require two-step approval (owner + security approver) before becoming active in Private deployments; approval events are logged.
REQ-07: Provide an operator-run read-only view that maps customer-facing audit events to internal service traces for troubleshooting without exposing raw cryptographic material.
REQ-08: All audit logs must be tamper-evident: include digest chaining or signed manifests to support forensic verification.
REQ-09: For HSM-backed master keys, the system must record a signed attestation of the HSM module model, firmware version, and the key's slot/identifier at provisioning time.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Demo: For a sample tenant, produce an audit export covering an SSO login, a role change, and a key rotation. Export must include correlation IDs and signed manifest.
AC-2: Automated test: RBAC change triggers a post-change smoke test that verifies access changes reflect expected permissions; test result is recorded in the audit ledger.
AC-3: Security validation: Independent security review validates tamper-evidence design (digest chaining or signatures) and confirms no plaintext keys are present in audit exports.
AC-4: Compliance signoff: Legal confirms exported artifacts meet evidence format requirements for customer audits (signed manifest with SHA-256 hashes and human-readable timeline).
AC-5: Performance: Audit export for a 24-hour high-traffic window (up to 1M events) completes within 6 minutes and produces a signed manifest.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta internal): Implement audit taxonomy, basic KMS event plumbing, and RBAC changelog. Deploy to internal Private testbed. (Owners: Eng-Security, Runtime).
Phase 2 (Customer pilot): Enable export and manifest signing, run pilot with 2 consenting enterprise customers and gather feedback. (Owners: Eng-Platform, Compliance).
Phase 3 (GA): Harden performance, add retention override UI in Console, and complete Legal/Compliance signoffs. (Owners: Product, Eng-Delivery).
test_plan: TP-1: End-to-end scenario test script covering SSO login, SAML logout, RBAC role swap, and KMS rotate; assert audit records are present and linked via correlation-id.
TP-2: Tamper-test: Modify an audit chunk and verify verification step detects alteration.
TP-3: Export validation: Request export for a correlation id and verify manifest signatures and included hashes match produced artifacts.
TP-4: Scalability test: Generate 1M synthetic events and measure export time and manifest generation latency.
signoff_checklist: Engineering: Implementation branch with tests, demo recording of export (link to PR)
Security: Architecture review completed and tamper-evidence design approved
Legal: Evidence artifact format accepted for customer audits
Compliance: Retention policy and deletion proof process documented
Product: Rollout plan and customer pilot identified
SRE: Runbook for export/recovery and incident playbook reviewed
Support: Knowledge base article and troubleshooting steps published
